clue.text: Vision with a funny hat on in the afternoon!

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters within the abbreviation for the afternoon

parts.note: PM, post meridiem, marks the afternoon

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters of hat and on are put into a peculiar new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a comical hat on seen in the afternoon, an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' looks like it describes the hat but signals the shuffle; 'in' puts the shuffled letters inside the afternoon abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is an apparition or ghostly sight, which is one sense of a vision.

clue.text: But farmers don't fail to make good turnover with it

definitions.text: But farmers don't fail to make good turnover with it

parts.words: But farmers don't fail to make good turnover with it
parts.note: the farm tool turns over the soil, and as slang the same word means to fail an exam, which farmers do happily

explanation.surface: A paradox about farmers earning good profits without failing.
explanation.walkthrough: In old British student slang, to be ploughed is to fail an examination; turnover is the soil turned, not the money.
explanation.definitionFit: The implement that turns over soil, and also old university slang for failing an exam.

clue.text: Merchant, dramatically in debt, is heavy-hearted

definitions.text: Merchant, dramatically in debt, is heavy-hearted

parts.words: Merchant, dramatically in debt, is heavy-hearted
parts.note: the title figure of Shakespeare's Venetian play borrows from Shylock and opens the play complaining of sadness

explanation.surface: A trader who owes money is feeling gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dramatically points to a play: Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice opens with this merchant saying he is sad, and he falls into Shylock's debt.
explanation.definitionFit: The merchant of Venice in Shakespeare's drama, melancholy and bound to Shylock for a loan.

clue.text: Keep turning this to crush the pig-nut !

indicators.note: to crush something is to break it up, so the letters of the pig-nut are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep turning a device to crack a pig-nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' rearranges THE PIGNUT. Keep turning this: what a screw or vice does as you turn it.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning a screw or vice repeatedly makes it firmer, so the phrasal verb means fasten more securely.

clue.text: Jerome's dog accompanied his trio

parts.note: the fox terrier who went with the three men in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat

explanation.surface: An author's dog that went along with his three friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerome K. Jerome's Three Men in a Boat follows three friends on the Thames, with a fox terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox terrier of Three Men in a Boat, the comic Thames novel by Jerome K. Jerome.

clue.text: A dance of father's — or his brother's?

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, so father's is pop's
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A party dance thrown by Dad, or perhaps by Dad's brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Father's brother is an uncle, old slang for a pawnbroker; to pop something is to pawn it, so a pop shop is a pawnshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, and a pawnbroker's place of business was nicknamed the pop shop.

clue.text: Mate gets the circuit set up of course

indicators.note: in a down clue set up turns the word upwards, so circuit is read bottom to top

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a racecourse

explanation.surface: A friend has the racing circuit laid out on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses LAP in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pal and mate are both informal words for a friend.

clue.text: A little butter an' maybe rice here in India

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter

indicators.note: maybe suggests another possible arrangement, so the letters of an are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small knob of butter and perhaps some rice, served in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges AN to NA. Patna is a city in India that gives its name to a long-grain rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Patna is a city in Bihar, India, famous for a long-grain rice named after it.

clue.text: He got roped in for many performances

definitions.text: He got roped in for many performances

parts.words: He got roped in for many performances
parts.note: a famous escapologist was tied up with ropes and chains on stage night after night

explanation.surface: Someone who was persuaded to take part in lots of shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Roped in looks like persuaded to join, but here it means literally tied up, as the great escape artist was.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the escape artist who freed himself from ropes, chains and handcuffs on stage.

clue.text: Unreasonable bylines ?

definitions.meaning: split as by lines: per is by and verse is lines of poetry

explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means contrary or unreasonable; split, it is per (by) and verse (lines).

clue.text: One more side for 50p would make it so

definitions.text: One more side for 50p would make it so

parts.words: One more side for 50p would make it so
parts.note: the British fifty-pence coin has seven sides, so adding a side gives a coin with eight

explanation.surface: A remark that the fifty-pence coin needs just one more side to be a certain shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The British 50p coin is a seven-sided shape (a heptagon); one more side makes eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight-sided is the meaning, and a heptagon plus one side has eight sides.

clue.text: More loyal than John Peel's hound ?

definitions.text: More loyal than John Peel's hound ?

parts.words: More loyal than John Peel's hound ?
parts.note: in the hunting song D'ye ken John Peel the hounds are Ranter, Ringwood, Bellman and True, so a comparative of loyal also reads as outdoing that dog

explanation.surface: Praise of someone more faithful than a famous huntsman's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a Cumbrian huntsman celebrated in an English folk song naming his hounds, one called True.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of faithful or loyal, which doubles as a jokey comparison with the hound named True.

clue.text: Wild cat found back in Montenegro

indicators.note: back tells us the hidden letters are read in reverse order
in signals letters sitting inside the country name Montenegro

explanation.surface: A wild feline discovered in the Balkan country of Montenegro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds TENEG inside MonTENEGro, and 'back' turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: The genet is a small spotted carnivore of Africa and southern Europe, a wild animal resembling a cat.

clue.text: Costume jewelry has a place, after brandy

indicators.note: after says the brandy comes first, with the a and place following it

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape skins left after pressing
a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: Fake jewellery comes with a setting, after a glass of brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcasite, crystals of iron pyrites cut and polished, is widely used in inexpensive fashion jewellery.

clue.text: Plots where the seed falls on stony ground

definitions.text: Plots where the seed falls on stony ground

parts.words: Plots where the seed falls on stony ground
parts.note: the parable of the sower has seed falling on stony ground; here the plots are garden beds built among stones

explanation.surface: An allusion to the parable of the sower whose seed lands on stony ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospel parable, seed falling on stony ground withers; in a garden of stones, plants are sown there on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden areas laid out with stones and alpine plants, where seed literally lands among rocks.

clue.text: German-type rustics?

parts.note: a cousin-german is a first cousin, so relations of that type living in the countryside are rural cousins

explanation.surface: A question about peasants of a Germanic sort.
explanation.walkthrough: German here is not the nationality: a cousin-german is an old term for a first cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated relatives from the provinces, with a nod to cousin-german meaning first cousin.

clue.text: One French work placed by common consent

parts.note: un is the French for one
op is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work
posed means put or placed in position

explanation.surface: A French work is agreed on by everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed with nobody against it has met no opposition from anyone.

clue.text: Secret store one dismantled in the City

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the postal code of the City of London

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London, the financial district

indicators.note: dismantled means taken apart, so the letters of store and one are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A hidden shop was taken apart in London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop but is anagram fodder; 'dismantled' shuffles it with the numeral, and 'in' sets the result inside the City of London's postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood by only a select few, so it is private or arcane.

clue.text: Elephants" dance-floor — a resort for philatelists?

definitions.meaning: a place where heavy animals tread and pound the earth
a favourite haunt, read jokingly as a place where people who collect postage labels gather

explanation.definitionFit: A favourite haunt is the idiom; read literally it is earth being trampled, or where stamp collectors gather.

clue.text: An unsociable person gets round many a social worker

parts.note: an becomes the indefinite article a

indicators.note: gets round means encircles, so loner wraps around the letter for many

parts.note: a loner prefers to be alone
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, which stands for many

explanation.surface: A withdrawn person wins over many a welfare worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets round' puts M inside LONER, giving LMONER, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a hospital social worker in Britain; originally an official giving alms.

clue.text: First appearance of Endymion's love

parts.note: in Greek myth the shepherd Endymion was loved by Selene, goddess of the lunar orb, whose first thin crescent appears each month

explanation.surface: The first sighting of a mythical shepherd's beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: Endymion was loved by Selene, the Moon; her monthly first appearance is the thin crescent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phase when the lunar crescent first appears, the moon being Endymion's lover Selene.

clue.text: " Their gee stinks ", said Laoconn

parts.note: Laocoon warned the Trojans against the wooden horse left by the besiegers, a gee being a horse

explanation.surface: A Trojan priest complains that someone's horse smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee (gee-gee) is a horse; Laocoon distrusted the Trojan horse, saying he feared the givers even bearing gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: The besiegers of Troy who left the wooden horse that Laocoon warned against.

clue.text: The Clemens boy making woodcuts?

definitions.meaning: the boy hero of Mark Twain's novel, Twain's real name being Samuel Clemens
a sawyer cuts wood, and tom is a male, so a male woodcutter

explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's boy hero; also, jokingly, a male sawyer, someone who cuts timber.

clue.text: A measure of noise east of Poplar

parts.note: the bel is a unit of sound intensity, ten decibels
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Measuring the noise level to the east of Poplar, a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar looks like the East London district, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar tree, a species of poplar.

clue.text: " The boast of heraldry, the pomp of — " (Gray)

definitions.text: " The boast of heraldry, the pomp of — " (Gray)

parts.words: " The boast of heraldry, the pomp of — " (Gray)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, whose line goes on with a word for might

explanation.surface: A missing word from a famous line of Thomas Gray's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The line from Gray's Elegy reads: The boast of heraldry, the pomp of power.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's missing word, which means might or authority.

clue.text: Kitchener's rank

definitions.meaning: a kitchener is an old word for a kitchen stove, so the kitchener's sort is a cooking stove
a rank is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen range is a cooking stove, once called a kitchener; a range is also a row, like a rank.

clue.text: Won't these muddlers take it to sharpen the wits ?

indicators.note: muddlers are things that jumble, so these letters of the words before are mixed up

explanation.surface: A suggestion that confused people should use a tool to sharpen their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddlers' rearranges the letters of WON'T THESE.
explanation.definitionFit: A whetstone is a stone for honing blades, and figuratively anything that hones the mind.

clue.text: Used to be putting heart back in 21

indicators.note: back says these central letters are read in reverse order
heart means the central letters of the answer to clue 21

parts.note: the answer to 21 across, Mark Twain's boy hero

explanation.surface: Something that once existed is restored to the heart of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle three letters, SAW, of 21 across, and 'back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Was is the past tense of be, so it means existed formerly.

clue.text: Old cavalry officers among the brass

definitions.meaning: the cornet was formerly the lowest commissioned rank in a British cavalry troop
brass instruments, the small trumpet-like ones in a band

explanation.definitionFit: A cornet was a junior cavalry officer who carried the colours, and also a valved brass instrument.

clue.text: These lines appear to suggest partiality

definitions.text: These lines appear to suggest partiality

parts.words: These lines appear to suggest partiality
parts.note: short railway tracks off the main line, whose name sounds like taking one side in a dispute

explanation.surface: Lines of writing that seem to show bias.
explanation.walkthrough: Railway lines branching off the main track also read as the act of taking sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Short tracks beside a main railway line, and also the act of backing one side in a quarrel.
